title: Protocol to detect in vitro and in cell ubiquitylation of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma by mitochondrial E3 ligase MITOL
protocol: Electrophorese lab-purified recombinant proteins MITOL (WT and CD) in SDS-PAGE.
Electrophorese known amounts of Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) protein on the same SDS-PAGE gel.
Stain the entire gel with Coomassie.
Determine the exact concentrations of MITOL WT and MITOL CD by comparing band intensity to the BSA gradient using a densitometer.
Incubate the mix at 30°C for 2 hours with mild shaking in a temperature-controlled mixer or circulating water bath.
Add 20 μL of 2×SDS loading dye to stop the reaction.
Mix well and boil the sample in boiling water or heat block (at 100°C) for 10 minutes.
Briefly spin down the samples.
Separate the samples on a 10% SDS PAGE gel.
Analyze ubiquitylation of substrate protein by Western blot using an antibody against Ubiquitin.
Determine that equal amounts of PolγA (WT or K1060R) were used with an anti-PolγA blot.
Seed 0.1 × 10^6 HEK293T cells in a 6-well cluster plate 24 h before transfection.
Grow the cells in a 37°C incubator with 5% carbon dioxide.
Pre-warm Opti-MEM media; keep plasmids and lipofectamine reagents ready for transfection.
Add 250 μL Opti-MEM to Tube A.
Add 1 μg Flag-PolγA, 1 μg Myc-MITOL WT, 1 μg MITOL CD, and 100 ng His-Ubiquitin plasmids to Tube A; mix well.
Add 250 μL Opti-MEM to Tube B.
Add a 1:3 ratio of Lipofectamine 2000 to Tube B.
Mix well.
Incubate the reaction at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Transfer the solution from Tube B to Tube A.
Mix well.
Incubate the reaction at room temperature inside the hood for 25 minutes.
Aspirate complete media from 6 wells in the cluster plate.
Add 1.5 mL Opti-MEM to the aspirated wells.
Add plasmids-Lipofectamine 2000 complex to the cells (total 500 μL per well).
Gently swirl and return the plate to the CO2 incubator.
After 6 hours, remove the Opti-MEM from the wells.
Replace it with complete media (2 mL per well).
Put back the cells in the incubator.
Prepare the lysate from cells 24 hours post-transfection.
Aspirate the media from the cells.
Wash the cells twice with 2 mL of ice-cold 1× PBS.
Add 200 μL/well of M2 lysis buffer supplemented with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail and PMSF (1 mM) to the cells.
Scrape and transfer the cells from each well to one tube.
Vortex the sample at high speed for 30 seconds.
Incubate the sample on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 17,000 × g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh prechilled tube and label it as cell lysate.
Check the protein concentration using Bradford or BCA protein estimation method.
Confirm expression of the proteins by Western blot before proceeding to immunoprecipitation.
Run cell lysates in a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membrane using Bio-Rad transfer apparatus with an overnight wet transfer protocol at 40 mA per gel for 16 h.
Block the membrane using 5% skim milk in 1× TBS + 0.1% Tween 20.
Incubate the membrane in anti-Flag (1:1,000 dilution) or anti-Myc antibody overnight with gentle rocking at 4°C.
Incubate blots in respective secondary antibodies (1:20,000 dilution) for an hour with gentle rocking at room temperature.
Wash the blots using an immobilon western chemiluminescent HRP substrate.
Develop the blots using an immobilon western chemiluminescent HRP substrate.
Equilibrate 5 μL of anti-Flag M2 affinity gel along with 10 μL of Sepharose CL6B in 500 μL M2 lysis buffer for 5 min.
Add the equilibrated anti-Flag M2 affinity beads and Sepharose CL6B to 100 μg–300 μg of cell lysates.
Make up the volume to 500 μL using M2 lysis buffer.
Incubate the sample at 4°C on an end-to-end rotor for 2 h.
Wash the beads three times at 226 × g, 4°C with 1 mL chilled M2 lysis buffer.
Remove the supernatant completely without disturbing the beads.
Add 10–20 μL of 2× SDS loading dye to the sample.
Boil the sample in boiling water for 10 min.
Check the pH of M2 lysis buffer if Flag tagged PolγA is not immunopurified optimally.
Increase the amount of anti-Flag M2 affinity gel to 7.5 μL or 10 μL per reaction if necessary.
Separate immunoprecipitated samples along with a pre-stained protein marker on a 10% SDS PAGE gel at 30 mA until the 18 kDa protein is visualized.
Transfer proteins from the gels to a 0.45 μm nitrocellulose membrane (Bio-Rad).
Block the membrane using 3% skim milk powder in 1×TBS + 0.1% Tween 20 for approximately one hour at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Incubate the membranes with anti-Flag antibody (1:2,000 in 1×TBS + 0.1%Tween 20) overnight at 4°C with gentle shaking to detect polyubiquitylation of PolγA.
Wash the membranes three times with 1×TBS + 0.1% Tween 20.
Incubate the membranes with anti-PolγA or anti-Ubiquitin antibodies (both at 1:1,000 in 1×TBS + 0.1%Tween 20) to detect polyubiquitylation of PolγA overnight at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Wash the membranes three times with 1×TBS + 0.1% Tween 20.
Incubate washed membranes with HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies (1:20,000 in 1×TBS+0.1% Tween 20) for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Wash the blots three times using 1×TBS+0.1%Tween 20.
Develop the blots using an immobilon western chemiluminescent HRP substrate.
Wash the membrane for 2 hours with 1×TBS+0.1% Tween 20 (every wash lasting 15 minutes).
Strip the blot with a commercially available stripping buffer for 15 minutes at 37°C if necessary.
Incubate the blot only with HRP-conjugated secondary antibody after stripping or washing.
Develop the blot to detect the antibody light chain.
